title: Per-endpoint performance briefing + rollout impact ribbon
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Goal: Design a compact, scannable 'briefing' panel for per-endpoint (route or model) performance that combines latency, throughput, token distribution, and a new rollout impact ribbon. This ticket delivers high-fidelity chart specs, interaction patterns, and a prototype for design review and engineering handoff.

Background: Operators want a single glance view to understand current health and recent rollout impact without drilling into long timelines. Existing route dashboards are powerful but require context switching between a timeline view and a separate rollouts tab. This design proposes a condensed briefing that sits above the full timeline and includes an interactive ribbon showing which deployments/rollouts affected metrics over the selected window.

Primary audiences: platform SREs, product engineers, customer success.

Core components to deliver:
- Briefing header: key KPI chips (p50/p95 latency, requests/s, avg tokens per generation, cost per 1k tokens) with micro-sparkline thumbnails.
- Metric panels: 3 small multiples (latency quantiles, throughput histogram, token-split stacked area).
- Rollout impact ribbon: a horizontal strip under metrics that maps release tags (canary, canary+fallback, stable) to colored bands; hover shows rollout metadata and linked PR/Runbook.
- Anomaly badges: transient flags (spike, regression, cost-surge) with severity color and one-click links to traces or evaluations.
- Timeline scrubber: shared X-axis with aggregation window control (1m/5m/1h) and quick-compare baseline toggle.
- Chart interactions: tooltip with breakdown by model variant, ability to pin a metric to top of Console, and export snapshot.

Design constraints and decisions made so far:
- Compactness prioritized: keep briefing to max 240px height so it fits above existing timeline without forcing a route-level page overflow.
- Quantiles chosen over mean for latency to reflect tail behavior relevant to SLOs.
- Rollout ribbon uses categorical color palette mapped to deployment tags; accessibility: colors pair with patterned overlay on hover.
- Cost overlay is optional and additive: toggled via chip to prevent clutter for users who only care about latency/throughput.

Engineering considerations included in spec: streaming data cadence (5s push), downsampling strategy for long-range views (LTTB for area charts, quantile sketches for latency), and expected circuit-breaker behavior when metric source is unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: Design reviewed by Console PM and SRE lead and sign-off recorded in comments
Prototype Figma file with responsive states (desktop and 1280px narrow) available
Chart spec sheet includes axes, aggregation window options, quantiles, sampling strategy, colors, and tooltip fields
Handoff tickets created for front-end (ENG) and telemetry (ENG) with mock assets and links
chart_specs: Latency chart: type=line with quantiles 0.5/0.9/0.99; Y-axis in ms (log toggle); X-axis shared time window; aggregation windows: 1m/5m/1h/24h; tooltip fields: timestamp, q50, q90, q99, sample_count, model_variant

Throughput chart: type=bar+line hybrid; bars = requests per aggregation window; line = moving average (5-window); Y-axis in requests/sec; histogram overlay mode for burst view; tooltip: req_count, peak_parallel, dropped_requests

Token distribution: type=stacked area; stacks = prompt_tokens / completion_tokens / cached_tokens; Y-axis = tokens/sec; color semantics: prompt (blue), completion (green), cache (amber); tooltip includes avg_tokens_per_request and 90th percentile token length
Rollout ribbon: categorical band chart; bands anchored to deploy timestamps; hover payload: deploy_id, commit_sha (short), rollout_percentage, health_checks_failed, linked PR URL

Anomaly badges: derived signals using z-score over baseline window; severity mapping: info/yellow (1.5-2.5), warn/orange (2.5-4.0), critical/red (>=4.0); tooltip: metric, deviation, suggested next action
